subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Suspension Bridge: Spanning the Impossible
description: A quick win: understand The Suspension Bridge: Spanning the Impossible.

hook.text: The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge in Japan spans 1,991 meters — nearly two kilometers of hanging roadway.

buildup.text: Two massive cables drape between towers. Vertical suspender cables hang the deck from the main cables.

discovery.text: The main cables are not single wires. They're bundles of 36,830 individual strands spun together on site.

twist.text: During construction, an earthquake struck. Engineers had to adjust the design while the bridge was partially built.

climax.text: The bridge withstands typhoons, earthquakes, and 23,000 vehicles daily. It was designed for all of them.

punchline.text: Two cables, 36,830 strands. That's how you cross the sea.

quiz.question: How many individual strands make up each main cable of the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge?
options: About 500 thick steel ropes woven together
Exactly 36,830 individual strands spun together on site
A single solid cable forged in a factory and shipped
